title: Plywood storage cube
summary: A storage cube of 18 mm birch plywood, 400 mm on each side. You cut five parts with a jigsaw, join them with glue and screws, and nail on a thin back.
priceNote: Example prices from a Dutch DIY store and timber merchant, with 21% VAT. Replace them with the prices at your store.

timber.name: Timber merchant
timber.note: Ask for birch plywood, grade BB/BB. Look at the two faces before you buy a sheet.

tools.name: Jigsaw blades
tools.spec: clean cut for wood (T101B), pack of 5

tools.name: Drill bit set
tools.spec: 2.5 mm and 4 mm wood bits, countersink bit

tools.name: Hammer
tools.spec: pin hammer or small claw hammer

jigsaw-guide.name: Cut along a guide with a jigsaw
jigsaw-guide.why: A jigsaw blade bends in thick plywood. A clamped guide and a slow push keep the cut straight.

warn.text: Keep your hands away from the area under the sheet. The blade comes out below the sheet.

do: Set the pendulum action of the jigsaw to 0.
Measure from the edge of the base plate to the near side of the blade.
Clamp the straightedge on the part side of the line, at that distance.
Put the base plate against the straightedge with the blade clear of the sheet.
Start the jigsaw.
When the blade is at full speed, push the jigsaw slowly along the straightedge.
Keep the base plate flat on the sheet until the cut is complete.

corner-clamp.name: Hold a corner with corner clamps
corner-clamp.why: A corner clamp holds two parts at 90°. Your two hands are then free for the drill.
do: Open the two jaws of the clamp wider than the parts.
Put the corner of the joint into the clamp.
Tighten the jaw on the first part.
Align the edges of the second part with the edges of the first part.
Tighten the jaw on the second part.

finish-brush.name: Brush a water-based finish
finish-brush.why: Thin coats dry fast and do not run. A thick coat stays soft and shows brush marks.

warn.text: Wear gloves. The finish can irritate your skin.
Do not shake the can. Air bubbles from the can stay in the dry finish.

do: Stir the finish for 1 minute.
Put one third of the brush hairs into the finish.
Brush a thin coat along the grain.
Brush each face from one end to the other in long strokes.
Remove runs at the edges with the brush.
Wait for the time on the can before the next coat.

steps.title: Cut the parts

warn.text: Wear safety glasses. The jigsaw can throw chips into your eyes.
Wear ear protection. A loud jigsaw can hurt your ears.
Keep your hands away from the area under the sheet. The blade comes out below the sheet.
Unplug the jigsaw before you change the blade. A saw that starts can cut you.
Put the sheet on the trestles with the good face down. The jigsaw splits the top face.

do: Put the 18 mm sheet on the two trestles with the good face down.
Mark each part from the cut list on the top face.

do.t: Measure each line two times before you cut.

do: Cut across the sheet first, at the end of each part.
Cut each piece to a width of 394 mm.
Cut back D from the 6 mm sheet the same way.
Write the part letter on the top face of each part.
steps.check: Make sure that you have two parts A and one each of parts B, C and D.
steps.why: A jigsaw cuts on the up stroke, so the bottom face stays clean. The face with the letter goes on the inside of the cube.
steps.tip: Keep the offcuts. They make good scrap blocks for the clamps and the drill.

steps.title: Sand the parts
do: Sand each cut edge to the line with 120 grit.
Sand the faces of each part with 120 grit.
Sand each sharp edge to a 1 mm round.
Sand all faces and edges again with 180 grit.
Remove the dust with a dry cloth.
steps.check: Make sure that the edges are straight and that no splinters show on the faces.
steps.why: Plywood edges show the plies. A smooth, round edge looks clean and does not splinter.
steps.tip: Keep the block flat on the edge. A tilted block makes the edge uneven.

steps.title: Drill the sides

warn.text: Put a scrap block under the side. The bit can split the face when it comes out.

do: Put the two sides A on the bench with the letters down.
Draw a line 9 mm from each short edge of each side.
Mark three holes on each line, at 40, 197 and 354 mm from a long edge.
Drill a 4 mm hole through the side at each mark.
Countersink each hole on the top face.
steps.check: Make sure that each side has six holes, 9 mm from the short edges.
steps.why: The line at 9 mm is the center of the 18 mm edge of the top and the bottom. Each screw then goes into the middle of the edge.

steps.title: Attach the bottom to a side

warn.text: Drill a pilot hole before you install each screw. A screw with no pilot hole splits the plies.

do.t: Put bottom B flat on the bench with the letter up.

do: Apply glue to one 394 mm edge of bottom B.
Put a side A against the glued edge, with its letter on the inside.
Align the holes in the side with the center of the edge.
Clamp the corner with the two corner clamps.
Drill a 2.5 mm pilot hole 25 mm into the edge through each hole.
Install three 40 mm screws through the side into the bottom.
steps.check: Make sure that the front edges of the side and the bottom are flush.
steps.why: The glue makes the joint strong. The screws pull the joint tight while the glue dries.

steps.title: Attach the top to the side

view.note: The picture shows the cube upright, as it stands at the end.

warn.text: When you drill, wear safety glasses. The bit can throw chips into your eyes.
Drill a pilot hole before you install each screw. A screw with no pilot hole splits the plies.

do: Turn the assembly upside down on the bench.
Apply glue to one 394 mm edge of top C.
Put top C flat on the bench with the letter up and the glued edge against side A.
Clamp the corner with the two corner clamps.
Drill a 2.5 mm pilot hole 25 mm into the edge through each hole.
Install three 40 mm screws through the side into the top.
steps.check: Make sure that the gap between the top and the bottom is 364 mm at the front and the back.

steps.title: Attach the second side

view.note: The picture shows the cube upright.

warn.text: When you drill, wear safety glasses. The bit can throw chips into your eyes.
Drill a pilot hole before you install each screw. A screw with no pilot hole splits the plies.

do: Put the assembly on the bench with side A down.
Apply glue to the free edges of the top and the bottom.
Put the second side A on the glued edges, with its letter on the inside.
Align the holes with the centers of the edges.
Drill a 2.5 mm pilot hole 25 mm into the edge through each hole.
Install six 40 mm screws through the side.
steps.check: Make sure that the front edges of the two sides, the top and the bottom are flush.
steps.tip: The weight of the side holds the joint, so you do not need the clamps.

steps.title: Attach the back

view.note: The picture shows the cube upright, from the back.

warn.text: Wear safety glasses. A pin can fly out of the wood when you hit it.

do: Put the cube on the bench with the front down.
Square the cube with the two diagonals.
Apply a thin line of glue to the back edges of the cube.
Put back D on the cube with the letter down and its edges flush with the outer faces.
Draw a line on back D, 9 mm from each edge.
Nail the back along the lines with 14 panel pins, about 100 mm apart.
steps.check: Make sure that no pin comes out of an inner or outer face of the cube.
steps.why: The back holds the cube square. The lines put each pin in the center of an 18 mm edge.

steps.title: Apply the finish

warn.text: Open a window or work outdoors. Finish fumes in a closed room can give you a headache.

do: Remove the dust from all faces with a damp cloth.
Brush the first coat on all faces, inside and outside.
Wait 2 hours.
Sand all faces lightly with 240 grit.
Remove the dust with a damp cloth.
Brush the second coat.
steps.check: Make sure that the finish is dry and smooth before you put items in the cube.
steps.why: Water lifts the wood fibres in the first coat. The light sand removes them, so the second coat is smooth.

steps.title: Attach the felt pads

view.note: The picture shows the cube upright, so you can see where each pad goes.

do: Put the cube upside down on a soft cloth.
Clean each corner of the bottom with a dry cloth.
Remove the paper from a felt pad.
Press the pad on a corner, 5 mm from each outer edge.
Attach the other three pads the same way.
steps.check: Make sure that the cube stands flat on the floor and does not rock.
steps.why: The pads keep the cube off the floor. They stop scratches on the floor and on the finish.
